item.title: Hurricane Isaias threatens Gulf Coast with rain, flooding. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, has strengthened into a Category 2 storm as it takes aim at the Gulf Coast from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: Trump promises not to resume Iran strikes before midterm elections
item.description: Crude oil prices had shot up on Thursday after reports President Trump was considering more strikes. They immediately dropped again after his new announcement.

item.title: Man shot by ICE agent in New York City's Marble Hill, authorities say
item.description: A man was hospitalized after being shot by an ICE agent in New York City's Marble Hill neighborhood, according to the DHS and city officials.

item.title: Mamdani, NYC officials give update on ICE shooting
item.description: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot and hospitalized a man in New York City on Thursday. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch gave an update on the situation, saying the victim's 5-year-old son was in the car during the incident.

item.title: LAUSD data shows student fights and threats higher than 4 years ago
item.description: Student fights and threats are still significantly up compared to four years ago, according to LAUSD data.

item.title: El-Sayed and Rogers toss insults in Michigan Senate debate
item.description: In Thursday's Michigan Senate debate, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers sparred over the Iran war and cost-of-living issues — and flung insults across the stage in nearly every exchange.

item.title: How affordability crisis impacts Americans' everyday lives – and how some are dealing with it
item.description: Trade wars, tariffs and the Iran conflict are hiking up costs for the everyday American. "CBS Evening News" takes a look at how it's impacting farmers, business owners and others around the country.

item.title: LAPD dog shootings raise questions about police tactics, best practice
item.description: CBS California Investigates looked at the LAPD's Use of Force reports over the past 10 years and found the LAPD had 19 cases in which officers shot at dogs in 2016. So far in 2026, there have been four incidents, resulting in three deaths.

item.title: Guilfoyle associate says when she asked him for $100K, it was "quid pro quo"
item.description: White House officials were told that text messages between Kimberly Guilfoyle and Eric Deters were real, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Pentagon will live stream Fort Hood shooter's execution, official says
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday said Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's execution by firing squad will be public. CBS News national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata reports. Then, legal contributor Jessica Levinson joins with analysis.

item.title: NFL urges Supreme Court to decide who should regulate prediction markets
item.description: In a legal brief, the NFL expressed support for prior court rulings favoring state authority to oversee prediction markets.

item.title: Experts say campus data undercounts sexual assaults
item.description: Sexual assaults are reported thousands of times a year on the biggest university campuses in the U.S., data shows. Experts say the data undercounts the number of incidents.

item.title: Judge presses Justice Department on justifications for White House media ban
item.description: Lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico were back in court as the legal battle continues over President Trump's decision to ban their reporters from the White House.

item.title: NFL urges Supreme Court to decide who should regulate prediction markets
item.description: The National Football League is now urging the Supreme Court to decide whether states should have the power to regulate prediction markets. Front Office Sports deals reporter Ben Horney joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Can GLP-1 drugs help people stop throwing away their money?
item.description: Researchers will explore whether weight-loss drugs can deter risky or impulsive financial decisions. "It might be very good financially for the average person," one neuroscientist said.

item.title: Teacher challenges students with $100 to get perfect chemistry exam score
item.description: A Long Island high school chemistry teacher promised a $100 prize to any student who could get a perfect score on the state's notoriously brutal chemistry exam. For the first time, one of his students succeeded. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Doctor explains how GLP-1 drugs could help reduce gambling, shopping addiction
item.description: Dr. Carolina Haass-Koffler, associate professor of psychiatry at Brown University, joins "The Daily Report" to explain how GLP-1 drugs could be used to treat addictions beyond excessive eating.

item.title: Florida bracing for impact from Hurricane Isaias
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall along the U.S. Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday. CBS News correspondent Jason Allen reports on the preparations. Then, meteorologist Darren Peck joins with the latest forecast.

item.title: Family of dead teen who was struck by deputy's car demands answers
item.description: Persephone Berger, 16, was pronounced dead after a deputy who was responding to a call about an unresponsive person lying in the road hit her with his vehicle.

item.title: Mississippi mayor details Hurricane Isaias preparations
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is the first storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season and is expected to make landfall sometime Friday or Saturday, threatening the Gulf Coast. Jay Willis, mayor of Pascagoula, Mississippi, joins to discuss how his town is preparing.

item.title: While waiting for Delta flight, police say man detoured, allegedly stole and crashed airport vehicle
item.description: Police say a Delta Air Lines passenger, bound for Seattle, decided to skip his flight, break out onto the tarmac of a Southern California airport and steal an airport vehicle. Kris Van Cleave reports on what happened next.

item.title: Riot police clash with students in Paris protests
item.description: In France, some public schools have been closed since Monday and won't reopen until next week amid nationwide student and labor protests that have been raging for three weeks. Aiden Stretch reports from Paris.

item.title: Family demands answers from police in teen's death
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Persephone Berger died on Saturday morning near St. Louis. Her family and friends are demanding to know why it took days to learn how she died. Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter's execution will be livestreamed, Pentagon says
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says the public will be able to watch the firing-squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the ex-Army major who was convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009.

item.title: USS Lincoln docks in San Diego, returning home for first time in 321 days
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln and its more than 4,500 sailors returned home to San Diego on Thursday for the first time in 321 days.

item.title: Trump says U.S. won't attack Iran before midterms
item.description: President Trump is saying the U.S. won't attack Iran again before the midterms as candidates face off in Georgia, Maine and Michigan in Thursday night debates. CBS News' political director Fin Gómez has more.

item.title: 10/8: CBS Evening News
item.description: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Category 2; Heroes' homecoming for USS Lincoln troops.

item.title: DOJ trying to indict former White House aide who testified about Jan. 6
item.description: Hutchinson, a former aide to White House chief of staff Mark Meadows, drew the ire of Trump's base when she testified in 2022 before the House Jan. 6 committee about Trump's actions that day.

item.title: What lies ahead for kids at center of California surrogacy investigation?
item.description: Guojun Xuan and Silivia Zhang were arrested on child abuse charges more than a year after 21 children were removed from their care.

item.title: Why you just got a $90 Social Security check — and who missed out
item.description: Millions of seniors are getting $90 direct deposits from Social Security this week, prompting questions about the source of the money.
